lines.text: Tinbergen saw it in the herring gull:
give the chick a painted stick more vivid than its mother's beak
and it pecks the stick, ignores the mother, starves for the brighter sign.
The magnolia is the painted stick.
It is more flower than any flower a beetle could dream,
and the beetle, dreaming, ferries genes it cannot see
toward an outcome it will never know.
